value: Whole-brain analysis comparing nicotine and placebo conditions revealed increased activation in regions encompassing the right frontopolar/anterior insula with nicotine administration (Nicotine–Placebo) for the Loss Cue–Neutral Cue contrast.
We also identified regions in bilateral superior frontal gyri, caudate, putamen, and dACC for the Loss Cue–Neutral Cue contrast, all with increased activation with nicotine.
Acute nicotine administration was associated with increased activation to cues anticipating rewards and losses in the right anterior insula, striatum, and dACC in a cohort of nonsmokers.

The nicotinic effect on insular activation to anticipatory cues for both gains and losses suggests that nicotine is associated with enhanced processing of salient cues regardless of valence, possibly by modulating interoceptive states associated with anticipating rewards and losses.

spans.text: Monetary Incentive Delay Task

description.value: Participants performed a monetary incentive delay task probing neural responses to anticipatory cues signaling possible monetary reward, loss avoidance, or neutral outcomes.

instructions.value: Respond using a button press as quickly as possible upon presentation of the target to gain or avoid losing money.

stimuli.value: Circle reward cues, square loss cues, triangular neutral cues, and a shaded white square target.

description.value: Participants discriminated between short and long mouths on cartoon faces while one stimulus was reinforced with monetary reward three times more often than the other, probing reward responsiveness through response bias.

instructions.value: Press “c” or “m” to indicate whether the face had the short or long mouth.

stimuli.value: Cartoon faces without mouths followed by briefly presented short or long mouths.
